obstacles: Raw voltage-dye micrographs and microelectrode calibration traces from the stage 15 Xenopus embryos are not deposited in a public repository.
Only the computational half of the claim can be re-verified from public resources without new wet-lab imaging.
rationale: The claim combines a computational prediction from the BETSE simulator with an in vivo calibrated voltage-dye measurement in Xenopus embryos. Because BETSE is open-source and the ionic and channel parameters are specified in the paper, the simulation prediction can be reproduced directly, whereas the raw in vivo imaging and patch/microelectrode calibration datasets are not publicly deposited.
